_about: Master findings register. Stable IDs: G-* from AUDIT-2026-09-01.md, N-* from AUDIT-2026-11-26.md. build.mjs renders this into the in-app Tested page and into FIXES-APPLIED-<buildDate>.md, so the page, the docs, and the gates cannot disagree. Do not hand-edit the generated files.

findings.title: Client system-role messages were forwarded to the model
findings.plain: Anyone could send the chat API a message labelled as coming from the system and override the assistant's instructions, turning the demo into a free general-purpose model on the project's key.
findings.technical: api/chat.js passed client messages through untouched. v3.0 whitelists roles to user and assistant, drops everything else, and caps length and count.
findings.before: attacker system message forwarded at index 1 of 2 system messages
findings.after: 0 client-controlled system messages; exactly one system message in every provider payload

findings.title: The deployed sales persona had no crisis clause
findings.plain: The red-team's first Critical fix (stop and point to emergency help if someone mentions self-harm) existed in the design doc and the offline prompt but had dropped out of the live sales prompt during a rewrite.
findings.technical: Personas now live in one file (backend/personas/personas.json) used by the server and injected into the page at build; a rule list (personas/rules.json) is asserted against every persona and the built page.
findings.before: sales persona: 0 crisis clauses
findings.after: 9 required rules present in both personas and in the built page

findings.title: Visitor knowledge-base edits could fill most of the system prompt
findings.plain: The 'edit the knowledge base' feature let a visitor push up to 36 edited passages of 1,500 characters each into the prompt with no marking, so 65% of what the model read could be visitor text.
findings.technical: Edits are now capped at 3 passages of 240 characters, control characters stripped, each labelled VISITOR-EDITED in the sources block, and the persona declares such passages untrusted data.
findings.before: 4,494 of 6,931 system-prompt bytes (65%) visitor-controlled, unlabelled
findings.after: at most 3 x 240 characters, labelled; attacker share under 20% in the gate

findings.title: Provider error bodies were echoed to the browser
findings.plain: When the model provider rejected a request, its raw error text (which can include key fragments and internal details) was sent to the visitor.
findings.technical: Provider errors are logged server-side; the client receives fixed honest copy with a short error code (model_unavailable, provider_rate_limited).
findings.before: HTTP 500 with the provider's 401 body including a key fragment
findings.after: HTTP 502/503 with fixed copy; provider text absent

findings.title: No guard against the assistant claiming it did something
findings.plain: The assistants cannot take actions, but a reply like 'I've processed your refund' rendered with no warning, and one phrasing even produced an affirmative ticket card.
findings.technical: A completion-claim guard flags first-person action claims and passive completion phrasing; the ticket card renders only when the visitor asked to escalate; a distinct 'Handed off (illustrative ticket)' badge replaces the misleading 'Not in knowledge base' badge on escalations.
findings.before: 20 of 20 phantom claims rendered with no specific warning; 1 got an affirmative card
findings.after: 20 of 20 flagged, 0 of 20 legitimate answers flagged, cards only with escalation intent

findings.title: Wildcard CORS and no security headers
findings.plain: Any website could call the demo's API from a visitor's browser, and the page shipped without the standard browser protections.
findings.technical: CORS now echoes only an explicit ALLOW_ORIGIN list (the same-origin page needs none). vercel.json is generated with a Content-Security-Policy whose script-src pins the SHA-256 of each inline script (computed by build.mjs), plus nosniff, frame-ancestors none, referrer and permissions policies.
findings.before: access-control-allow-origin: *; no headers block
findings.after: no ACAO without an allowlist; CSP with per-script hashes; 5 protective headers
findings.gate: test/gate-static.mjs: CSP hashes match built scripts; test/gate-endpoint.mjs: CORS

findings.title: On a phone the first screen had no chat
findings.plain: After 'Enter the demo' a phone visitor saw badges, picker cards and a tips popup; the chat was almost two screens down.
findings.technical: Under 640px the layout is chat first: compact hero, picker as a horizontal strip, sidebar after the chat, tips popup suppressed, min-width 0 on grid items.
findings.before: chat top at 1,409px on an 844px viewport
findings.after: chat visible in the first screen on 390x844 (gate asserts chat top below viewport height)

findings.title: Docs claimed things the code did not do
findings.plain: README and design docs said the sales bot books demos, every answer is cited, a faithfulness check runs, the RAG toggle works, and the prompts are used verbatim. None of those were true of the deployed site.
findings.technical: README, backend README, DEPLOY-GUIDE rewritten; design docs and June test reports marked historical; the static gate forbids the specific overstatements.
findings.before: 9 unsupported claims
findings.after: 0 forbidden claim strings in the docs (gate list)

findings.title: The repo contained no tests and no CI
findings.plain: The project described itself as tested, but a clean clone had nothing to run.
findings.technical: Root package.json with npm test (build, static gate, endpoint gate, UI gate, retrieval eval, audit probe), declared devDependencies, GitHub Actions workflow.
findings.before: 0 test files, no package.json, no workflow
findings.after: 5 gates plus the eval and the probe run on every push

findings.title: 271 em and en dashes, including the title
findings.plain: A project rule forbids dashes in copy, docs and code comments; the repo had 271 across 19 files.
findings.technical: Full sweep; the static gate fails on any em or en dash in the repo.
findings.before: 271 dashes in 19 files

findings.title: Switching bots mid-reply misfiled the answer
findings.plain: Ask Support a question, switch to Sales before the reply arrives, and the Support answer showed up in the Sales transcript.
findings.technical: send() captures the bot at send time and appends the reply to that bot's history; the DOM updates only if that bot is still active.
findings.before: answer shown in the other transcript
findings.after: answer stays with the bot that was asked

findings.title: A suggestion clicked while busy erased the draft
findings.plain: Clicking a sidebar suggestion while a reply was pending overwrote whatever you were typing and sent nothing.
findings.technical: Suggestions route through ask(): if a reply is pending the suggestion is queued and runs after it; drafts are never overwritten.
findings.before: draft replaced, suggestion dropped
findings.after: draft preserved, suggestion queued and sent

findings.title: Controls that did nothing on the live site
findings.plain: The RAG toggle and the API-key gear were visible but ignored when the backend was in use, and a TOP_K setting was read and never applied.
findings.technical: Both controls are hidden in backend mode (body.backend-mode); TOP_K is applied (default 3, max 6).
findings.before: RAG off still cited; gear save changed nothing; TOP_K unused
findings.after: controls hidden; TOP_K respected

findings.title: The identity check could not be completed by a visitor
findings.plain: The support bot asks for an email on file and a workspace URL, but nothing on the page told visitors what to type.
findings.technical: A demo-account card in the support sidebar shows owner@acme-co.example and acme-co with honest copy that the check is illustrative and low-assurance.
findings.before: 0 hints on the page
findings.after: demo values on screen next to the chat

findings.title: Over-escalation and a stretched discount
findings.plain: Asking whether there is a phone number produced a ticket instead of the honest answer that support is by email, and the student-discount answer extended an institutional discount to students.
findings.technical: Persona rules added: a question about how to reach support is a question, not a request; published discounts are never extended to unnamed groups. Escalations now carry a Handed off badge instead of Not in knowledge base.
findings.before: ticket 3 of 3; over-extension 2 of 3 (live)
findings.after: rules shipped; live repeats pending after deploy
findings.status: fixed in prompt, live verification pending

findings.title: Rate limit keyed on a client-writable header
findings.plain: The fair-use limiter read the first value of x-forwarded-for, which a client can prepend to.
findings.technical: clientIp() prefers x-real-ip and otherwise the last hop of x-forwarded-for, the one the platform appends.
findings.before: 25 requests with a rotating prefix, never limited
findings.after: limited at request 21 regardless of prefix

findings.title: Question words polluted keyword retrieval
findings.plain: Words like 'what' were not stopwords, so a passage headed 'What is included' could rank for 'what is your refund policy'.
findings.technical: Shared retriever with an extended stopword list and a rule that a single common term is not evidence; the same module runs on the server and in the page.
findings.before: junk keyword-only chunk in top 3
findings.after: 0 keyword-only junk for the gate query; page and server rank identically
findings.gate: test/gate-endpoint.mjs: junk keyword; test/gate-static.mjs: injected retriever equals module

findings.title: Ticket IDs repeated across visitors
findings.plain: The model was inventing ticket numbers and kept reusing the same few.
findings.technical: The server generates a random NIM id per request and instructs the model to use exactly that id; the gate asserts two requests get different ids.
findings.before: 4 distinct IDs in 10 escalations
findings.after: unique per request

findings.title: Retrieval quality had no evidence
findings.plain: There was no gold set and no published number; the page's suggested questions reuse knowledge-base wording, so any number on them would be optimistic.
findings.technical: eval/gold.json (30 items: paraphrases, vocabulary matches, and out-of-scope questions) runs through the shipped retriever; keyword-path recall is stamped into the page at build and labelled in-sample-adjacent; the hybrid number requires a live key and is reported as not yet measured until eval/run.mjs is run with API_KEY.
findings.before: no gold set, no number
findings.after: gold set shipped, keyword-path recall stamped, held-out protocol documented
findings.status: partially fixed: hybrid number pending a live run

findings.title: Voice endpoint usable as anonymous speech-to-text
findings.plain: Anyone could post audio to the transcription API without loading the demo.
findings.technical: A short-lived page token (issued by GET /api/health, HMAC of a timestamp, 15 minute life) is required; daily ceiling lowered to 150 per instance. This is a friction control, not authentication, and is described as such.
findings.before: anonymous POST accepted
findings.after: 401 without token; 200 with the page token

findings.title: Keyboard and navigation gaps
findings.plain: Escape did not close the source drawer, there were no direct links to the X-ray or the evidence page, and the tips popup covered the phone layout.
findings.technical: Escape closes the drawer and the modal; #kb, #xray, #tested and #chat deep links skip the cover; tips are hidden under 640px.
findings.before: drawer open after Escape; no deep links
findings.after: Escape closes; deep links work

findings.title: No version stamp and an unreproducible card image
findings.plain: The page carried no version, the package version never changed, and the social card was generated by a script that was not in the repo.
findings.technical: version.json feeds the page stamp, the health endpoint, and the card; tools/og-image.py is committed; CHANGELOG.md added.
findings.before: no stamp; generator absent
findings.after: v3.0.0 stamped; generator committed
findings.gate: test/gate-static.mjs: version stamp and generator present

findings.title: No link to the sister project
findings.plain: The page and README did not mention the Harlan & West project built with the same method.
findings.technical: Footer and README cross-link via the sisterUrl field in version.json.
findings.before: no mention
findings.after: cross-linked

findings.title: X-ray copy overstated its scope
findings.plain: The README promised the X-ray scores the whole knowledge base; it showed ten passages.
findings.technical: The endpoint now returns all 36 passages with scores; the page shows ten and offers Show all.
findings.before: 10 of 36 returned
findings.after: 36 returned, 10 shown, fold for the rest

findings.title: One client could lock every visitor out for a day
findings.plain: Rejected requests still counted against the shared daily budget, so a single script could take the free demo offline for everyone on a server instance.
findings.technical: lib/limits.mjs checks the caller first and counts only accepted requests; each address also gets a daily share (120 chat, 30 voice) and the log notes 80% and 100% of the budget. A Vercel WAF rate-limit rule in front of it is a dashboard step (DEPLOY-GUIDE.md).
findings.before: 600 requests from one IP, then a new visitor got 429
findings.after: attacker limited at request 21, rejected requests spend nothing, a new visitor is served

findings.title: A knowledge-base edit steered the bot into asking for card numbers
findings.plain: A visitor's own edit to a passage could make the assistant tell them to email a full card number. It only affects the editor's session, but it is the injection path a shared knowledge base would open.
findings.technical: Phase 1 guard layer: deterministic output rules block any reply that asks for card numbers, passwords or codes (R-SECRET) and remove emails, links and phone numbers that are not in the original knowledge base or the visitor's own messages (R-CONTACT). A request carrying visitor edits is answered as checked JSON, never streamed, the answer is tagged 'Uses your edit', and the source drawer shows the original passage beside the edit.
findings.before: 1 of 2 live runs asked for a card number
findings.after: card-number request replaced by the safe reply; injected contact removed; edits never streamed

findings.title: Personal data and the Gemini free tier
findings.plain: Google's terms ask that personal information not be sent to its unpaid tier, and the sales bot asked for names and work emails.
findings.technical: A privacy note now sits under the composer and on the intro, the sales persona suggests example values (Alex Example, alex@example.com), and the 'free AI quota' copy is gone. Attaching billing to the key's Cloud project is an owner step.
findings.before: names and emails requested; voice clips sent; free-tier copy in the UI
findings.after: privacy note shipped, example values suggested; paid tier pending the owner
findings.gate: test/gate-ui.mjs: N-03 privacy note; persona drift gate
findings.status: partially fixed: paid tier is an owner step

findings.title: The support bot printed its own instructions
findings.plain: Asked for its system prompt, the bot printed it verbatim despite a rule against it. The prompts are public in the page source, so nothing secret leaked, but the rule was not true.
findings.technical: An output rule replaces any reply that overlaps the bot's own instructions verbatim (R-PROMPT, four or more shared 8-word runs), and the sidebar links the published prompts, since they are public by design.
findings.before: live reply matched the persona verbatim
findings.after: recitation replaced; prompts linked as public

findings.title: The student discount was still stretched (G-15)
findings.plain: The sales bot told a college student the institutional education discount applied to them.
findings.technical: The sales persona names the case, and an output rule (R-STUDENT) appends the institutional rule to any reply that tells a student the education discount applies. Gold-set questions added; a live rerun remains.
findings.before: 2 of 2 live runs over-extended
findings.after: rule appended deterministically; prompt rule shipped
findings.status: fixed in prompt and output rule, live verification pending

findings.title: Plural questions missed the pricing passages
findings.plain: Asking 'What plans do you offer?' retrieved security and refund passages, because 'plans' never matched 'plan'.
findings.technical: Light plural stemming in the shared tokenizer, a common term counts as evidence when it is in the passage heading, and fusion drops keyword-only hits under 40% of the best keyword score. Plural cases added to eval/gold.json.
findings.before: keyword top-3: security.hipaa, data.export, billing.refunds
findings.after: pricing passages ranked for the plural question; keyword recall@3 0.73 to 0.81 on a larger gold set

findings.title: A malformed voice token crashed the function
findings.plain: A broken page token made the voice endpoint fail with a server crash instead of a polite refusal.
findings.technical: verifyToken validates the shape and length before comparing, never throws, and every malformed token is a 401.
findings.before: live 500 FUNCTION_INVOCATION_FAILED
findings.after: 401 for every malformed shape tested

findings.title: Earlier assistant turns can be forged
findings.plain: The browser sends the chat history, so a visitor can write a fake earlier reply and the model treats it as its own.
findings.technical: Every answer leaves the server with an HMAC over the bot and the exact text; the page sends it back, and assistant turns without a valid signature (forged, edited, or from the other bot) are dropped before the model sees them.
findings.before: forged turn forwarded to the model
findings.after: forged and tampered turns dropped; genuine signed turns kept, streamed or not

findings.title: One request could carry 164,000 characters
findings.plain: A single request could push a whole novel's worth of text to the model, and an empty request still cost a model call.
findings.technical: Requests are capped at 12 turns and 12,000 characters (oldest turns drop first), a request without a visitor message is a 400 before any provider call, and each request logs counts only.
findings.before: 164,326 characters forwarded; empty POST made one provider call
findings.after: at most 12 turns and 12,000 characters; empty request refused with no provider call

findings.title: Server files were served as public URLs
findings.plain: The server code, prompts and knowledge-base JSON could be downloaded from the live site.
findings.technical: Only backend/public/ is the static root (vercel.json outputDirectory). Server code, prompts and the knowledge base are bundled into the functions, and unknown paths get a 404 page.
findings.before: /lib/security.mjs, /personas/*.json, /kb.json and others returned 200
findings.after: 404 for every server path; public assets still served

findings.title: Dark mode failed text contrast
findings.plain: Blue accent text, the Live badge and the phone Send button were too faint to read comfortably.
findings.technical: Accent is split into a fill token (white text on it is at least 4.5:1) and an ink token for accent-coloured text; light-mode green and badge colours were darkened.
findings.before: up to 26 failing elements per view
findings.after: axe: no serious issues in any view, theme or phone

findings.title: Keyboard focus escaped the intro and the source drawer
findings.plain: Tabbing on the intro reached hidden controls behind it, and opening a source did not move focus to it.
findings.technical: The page behind the intro is inert until you enter; the source drawer is a labelled modal dialog that takes focus, keeps Tab inside, and returns focus to the citation on close.
findings.before: focus behind the cover after 5 Tab stops; drawer had no dialog role
findings.after: focus stays in the intro; drawer takes and returns focus

findings.title: The model is legacy-gated and unmonitored
findings.plain: The default model is only served to existing Gemini users, and nothing checks that it still answers.
findings.technical: Request bodies are model-aware (Gemini 2.5 thinking off; Gemini 3 at its defaults with token headroom), /api/health?deep=1 runs a cached canary call that drives the status pill, and a daily GitHub Action checks the live model. Switching CHAT_MODEL to Gemini 3.5 Flash-Lite and rerunning the live eval is an owner step.
findings.before: /api/health reports the model but never calls it
findings.after: canary drives the pill and runs daily; model switch ready
findings.status: partially fixed: switching CHAT_MODEL is an owner step

findings.title: On phones the composer started below the fold
findings.plain: After entering on a phone, the message box sat off screen and many controls were small to tap.
findings.technical: On phones the chat card fills the rest of the first screen with the composer in view, and every control is at least 44 px.
findings.before: composer below the fold at 390x844; 21 controls under 44 px
findings.after: composer in view at 360x740, 375x667 and 390x844; 0 controls under 44 px

findings.title: The voice endpoint read any file type
findings.plain: The transcription endpoint would pass images or PDFs to the model, making it a free document reader.
findings.technical: Only WAV audio is accepted: the declared type must be WAV and the bytes must start with a RIFF/WAVE header.
findings.before: application/pdf forwarded with 200
findings.after: 415 for PDF and for non-WAV bytes labelled WAV

findings.title: Invisible Unicode passes into prompts
findings.plain: Hidden tag characters, zero-width and direction controls reach the model unchanged.
findings.technical: Visitor messages and edits are NFKC-normalized and stripped of tag characters, zero-width and bidi controls and variation selectors; requests that contained them are counted in the logs.
findings.before: all three survive into the prompt
findings.after: no invisible characters reach the model

findings.title: Citation lists showed as raw text, even on a refusal
findings.plain: Answers citing '[S1, S2, S3]' showed the raw markers, and one was attached to a refusal.
findings.technical: Citation lists render as one button per source, and both personas say citations belong only on facts taken from the sources.
findings.before: raw '[S1, S2, S3]' on a refusal
findings.after: three citation buttons, no raw markers; refusal rule in both personas
findings.status: fixed in code and prompt, live verification pending

findings.title: Bad JSON was reported as a model outage
findings.plain: A malformed request got a 'model unavailable' error instead of telling the caller the request was wrong.
findings.technical: Both endpoints parse the body defensively and answer 400 invalid_json.
findings.before: 502 model_unavailable
findings.after: 400 invalid_json

findings.title: The intro animation kept running after entering
findings.plain: A timer on the hidden intro kept animating in the background.
findings.technical: The pipeline animation runs only while the intro is visible and the tab is in view.
findings.before: 14 class changes in 5 s while hidden
findings.after: 0 changes after entering

findings.title: Dead bring-your-own-key code shipped
findings.plain: Hidden settings for pasting an OpenAI or Anthropic key, and stale copy, were still in the production page.
findings.technical: The modal, gear, RAG toggle and third-party model calls are removed; only the embedding adapter used by the UI gate remains.
findings.before: hidden modal and browser calls to OpenAI and Anthropic
findings.after: 0 dead controls, 0 third-party model URLs

findings.title: No security.txt, crawler files or CSP reporting
findings.plain: There was no standard place to report a vulnerability, no robots or sitemap, and no way to learn about blocked content.
findings.technical: RFC 9116 security.txt (GitHub private advisories), robots.txt, sitemap.xml, a counts-only /api/csp-report endpoint, COOP and CORP same-origin, and no-store on the API.
findings.before: 404 or absent
findings.after: served; CSP violations logged as directive, origin and path only

findings.title: The voice-token secret came from the API key
findings.plain: Rotating the model key and rotating the page-token secret were the same act.
findings.technical: A separate TOKEN_SECRET is used whenever it is set; until the owner sets it, the old derivation keeps deployments working.
findings.before: secret = hash of the provider key
findings.after: TOKEN_SECRET supported and gated
findings.status: partially fixed: set TOKEN_SECRET in Vercel

findings.title: Missing landmarks, skipped headings, a tips card over content
findings.plain: Screen-reader navigation lacked a main region, heading levels skipped, and the tips popup covered the page for 13 seconds.
findings.technical: Header, main and footer landmarks; headings in order; the intro is a labelled dialog; tips are docked in the sidebar and remembered once dismissed.
findings.before: axe landmark-one-main, region, heading-order
findings.after: axe: no serious issues

findings.title: A link was told apart by colour only
findings.plain: The audit link on the Tested page looked like the surrounding text except for its colour.
findings.technical: Links inside running text are underlined.
findings.before: link-in-text-block 1.44:1
findings.after: underlined
